clue.text: Painter's finish in black, also in blue

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its closing letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

parts.note: last letter of the colour word
also and and both add something further
sky blue, the colour of a clear sky

explanation.surface: A painter puts the finishing touches to a canvas in black and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking the painter to the wordplay; 'finish in black' reads like painting technique but just takes the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassily Kandinsky was a Russian abstract artist, a pioneer of non-representational painting.

clue.text: Do joint — and drink

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
to sup is to sip a drink

explanation.surface: Smoke a joint and have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A do and a knees-up are both British informal words for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A knees-up is a lively informal party with dancing, which is what a do means in casual British speech.

clue.text: Boy, after upset, took heart from fresh love match

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A distraught boy took heart from a new romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is nil in sport, so a love match is a game ending nil-nil.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-score draw is a football result where neither side scores, a nil-nil game.

clue.text: One sent off for smaller map

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters go out of their order

explanation.surface: One person is dismissed in exchange for a smaller map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent off' reads as dismissed, but 'off' is the rearranging signal for sent alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small map placed within a larger one, often to show detail or location.

clue.text: Seafood good with starter of eggs and mash?

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A seafood dish served with an egg starter and mashed potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mash' looks like potato on the menu; it is the verb, to squash.
explanation.definitionFit: To squidge is to squash or squeeze something soft, much as one would mash it.

clue.text: Informal agreement essential to stay ahead

indicators.note: what is essential to a phrase lies at its core, inside its letters

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: An informal deal that is vital for keeping in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Yah is a casual, upper-class British way of saying yes, an informal word of assent.

clue.text: One may have the landlord to answer to

definitions.text: One may have the landlord to answer to

parts.words: One may have the landlord to answer to
parts.note: surface reading: a tenant who must account to the person they rent from
setter's reading: a pub contest where the publican asks the questions and drinkers supply answers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Answer to' suggests being accountable to a landlord who owns your flat; the landlord here runs a pub and sets questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiz night in a bar is often hosted by the licensee, who reads out the questions for teams of drinkers.

clue.text: Trainer repeated test: moan goes up

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading from the bottom to the top

explanation.surface: A coach groans as an exam has to be retaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainer' could be a shoe; it is one who practises a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A practiser is someone who drills or exercises a skill, so the word fits one who trains.

clue.text: Transport for London youth includes something with wings

indicators.note: includes means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for the capital's transport authority

explanation.surface: London's transport authority takes on a young man who flies about.
explanation.walkthrough: TfL is Transport for London, which runs the city's buses and Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A botfly is a hairy fly whose larvae live as parasites in mammals, so it is a winged insect.

clue.text: Song — woefully unrehearsed — then chat

indicators.note: woefully means badly, so the letters are put together badly in a new order

parts.note: all the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A singer performs a number badly unprepared, then chats to the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath the Arches is a 1930s music-hall song made famous by Flanagan and Allen.

clue.text: Final letter and one poem that won't offend a number in US

parts.note: the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The last letter and one inoffensive verse make an American number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poem that won't offend' is a PC ode: the qualifier comes before the noun in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A zip code is the numeric postal code used by the American mail service to route letters.

clue.text: ME city fears a backlash after withdrawing exhibits

indicators.note: withdrawing is pulling back, so the letters are read backwards
the phrase exhibits, or puts on show, a word sitting inside its letters

parts.note: the letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: People in a Middle Eastern city dread a backlash after troops pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is the standard abbreviation for Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Basra is Iraq's main port city in the south of the country, near the Gulf.

clue.text: Martial arts standard British have to beat

parts.note: to belt is to hit hard

explanation.surface: British fighters must beat a martial arts benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo and karate the brown belt is a grade just below black, marking a rank of skill reached.

clue.text: Looking to incorporate charge for major promotion

indicators.note: incorporating something takes it into the body, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bill is a charge to pay

explanation.surface: Seeking to include a fee in exchange for a big career move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' suggests a step up at work; it is publicity on a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Star billing puts a performer's name most prominently on posters, the top place in advertising a show.

clue.text: Area near vessel that's very deep

definitions.note: a noun phrase: something that's very deep

explanation.surface: The sea area next to a ship is very deep water.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a chasm or gulf so profound it seems bottomless, a thing of great depth.

clue.text: She sets out at a different point

indicators.note: a different version of these letters is a new arrangement of them

parts.note: every letter of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: A woman heads off and arrives somewhere other than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' is part of the letters; the definition is the single last word, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: East-southeast is one of the sixteen named directions marked on a compass rose, between east and southeast.

clue.text: Tact of detective, quick to accept large award

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A detective shows tact, rushing to accept a big prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour in the monarch's personal gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomacy means handling people sensitively, which is exactly what tact is.

clue.text: Cut down with small saw

parts.note: a potted history is a shortened, abridged one

explanation.surface: A tree is felled using a little saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the cutting tool of the surface, but it is the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, so spotted is a past-tense synonym of saw.

clue.text: Gossip increasingly tawdry when one's left

indicators.note: one is swapped so that the left abbreviation takes its place

parts.note: more tatty, the comparative of a word for shabby

explanation.surface: Gossip grows ever more sordid once someone has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the I in TATTIER with L to get TATTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler tells tales and spreads rumours, so it is a person who gossips.

clue.text: Meal out whose attendees presumably didn't stuff themselves

definitions.text: Meal out whose attendees presumably didn't stuff themselves

parts.words: Meal out whose attendees presumably didn't stuff themselves
parts.note: surface reading: an outing where the diners showed restraint and did not overeat
setter's reading: the guests are soft toys, filled with stuffing by someone else

explanation.walkthrough: The picnickers are soft toys from a well-known children's song; they were stuffed by a toymaker, not by eating.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1907 song describes toy bears gathering in the woods for an outdoor feast, a meal eaten outside.

clue.text: Works together, wrestling to pull in shed to the left

indicators.note: in an across answer, going to the left means reading right to left
pulling something in draws it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away, or shed it

explanation.surface: Wrestlers co-operate to drag a garden shed along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like the noun of the surface but is a verb, discard.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition gathers several works, such as novels or episodes, into a single volume or broadcast.

clue.text: Urge to let on about official statement

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
to let a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: An urge to reveal information about an official announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let on about' reads as reveal, but 'on' places the let word after the about word.
explanation.definitionFit: A press release is a formal announcement issued to journalists by an organisation.

clue.text: Threat to visibility from different directions a worry

parts.note: south and east, two compass points

explanation.surface: A worry coming from all sides threatens one's sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a cold mist rolling in off the North Sea onto the British east coast, which cuts down how far one can see.

clue.text: Judge in working party sprang up, nicely stoned?

indicators.note: in places the first piece within the next

parts.note: a bee is a gathering of people working together, as in a sewing bee
water wells up when it springs from the ground

explanation.surface: A judge at a work party leapt up, pleasantly high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' suggests drugs; here it means set with precious stones. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bejewelled is decorated with gems, so it has been prettily adorned with stones.

clue.text: Figure on fencing team gets drug

indicators.note: fencing something in surrounds it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: eleven, the size of a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: A figure on a fencing team is caught using drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests the sport; it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitoxin is a heart medicine extracted from foxglove, used to treat heart failure.

clue.text: Grasped small volume in wonderment

parts.note: centilitre, a small measure of liquid

explanation.surface: Someone understood a slim book and was amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like an insertion signal, but 'in wonderment' together means awed.
explanation.definitionFit: To claw at something is to seize it with nails or talons, so clawed means seized hold of.

clue.text: Island's empty reservoir, something sheep go around

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so one piece holds the other
an empty word has lost its inside, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An island's reservoir has run dry, and sheep wander round it.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is'. 'Something sheep' is short for something sheep say.
explanation.definitionFit: Barra is one of the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast, famous for its beach airstrip.

clue.text: Lord's lady out to lunch with Arab withholding tip

indicators.note: withholding the tip keeps back an end, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A peer's wife is away at lunch with an Arab who keeps the gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, so its lady is a female cricketer at the crease, not a peer's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A batswoman is a female cricketer who bats, the kind of player seen at the home of cricket.

clue.text: One warning of dangerous bend that's brief hindrance for car

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: chevron road signs warn of a sharp bend
as in 'without let or hindrance', let means obstruction

explanation.surface: A road sign warning of a sharp bend briefly holds up a motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: Let as hindrance survives in tennis and on British passports ('without let or hindrance').
explanation.definitionFit: Chevrolet is an American automobile brand owned by General Motors, so its name is a make of vehicle.

clue.text: My rugby training base

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: A rugby team's training ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a training ground; it is the adjective, morally low.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low and dishonourable, and corrupt describes someone who is dishonest and debased.

clue.text: Calling a bird a fish

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly calls a bird a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' looks like part of the surface naming, but it is the definition: naming, giving a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Titling something is giving it a name, so it matches calling in the sense of naming.

clue.text: Caught on top of tower, told off

parts.note: to wig someone is to scold them

explanation.surface: Someone stuck on top of a tower gets scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught on' suggests being snagged; it means understood. To twig is British slang for realising.
explanation.definitionFit: Twigged is informal British for realised or understood, the same as caught on to an idea.

clue.text: Drag performer tailed Irish girl in London landmark

indicators.note: to tail something here is to remove its tail, so the end letter goes

parts.note: one who drags or tows something

explanation.surface: A drag queen follows an Irish girl around a famous London sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag performer' suggests a drag act; it is a literal one who drags, a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower Bridge is the Victorian bascule bridge over the Thames beside the Tower of London.

clue.text: Fearful dinner periodically must upset stomach

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned over, so read from the bottom

parts.note: the even-placed letters of the two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like the belly; it is the verb, to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to put up with it, the same as to tolerate or bear it.

clue.text: Wig this thin, anyhow is visible

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the letters are put in a careless new order

parts.note: all the letters of the three words

clue.text: To star as revolutionary attracted American

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests revolving, turning the letters round to read backwards

explanation.surface: An American drawn to play the lead role as a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like the lead actor; it is the Sun, the star we orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunward means towards the Sun, and the Sun is our nearest star, so it means heading to a star.

clue.text: Frequently studied words of praise for hitchhiker?

second meaning: compliments on how skilfully someone stuck out a thumb for a lift

clue.text: Poll advises changing filming technique

indicators.note: changing the letters alters their order into something new

parts.note: all the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A survey recommends a new way of shooting a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap dissolve is a cinema transition where one shot fades out while the next fades in over it.

clue.text: Drive to Spar to collect border sprinkler

indicators.note: collecting something gathers it in, so one piece is held within the others

explanation.definitionFit: A dredging box is a kitchen container with a perforated lid for shaking flour or sugar over food.

clue.text: Poles tend not to have male heraldic line

explanation.definitionFit: A bar sinister is a diagonal band on a coat of arms, popularly taken as a mark of illegitimacy.

clue.text: Most down pint finally after second helpings of pastry

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

clue.text: Dear old writer's English verse I recalled

parts.note: an ex is a former one

clue.text: Staff that worked miracles with radar soon relocated

parts.note: all the letters of the two words

explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Aaron's rod was the stick that miraculously turned into a snake and later blossomed.

clue.text: Variable in length, containing nothing that's illuminating

something variable can take different forms, so the letters vary their order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable' suggests the maths letter, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A neon light is a glowing gas-filled tube, a lamp that lights up, used in shop signs.

clue.text: Article that's round supporting front of stage

indicators.note: being round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

clue.text: Secure language for digital application

clue.text: Error excluding metaphors

clue.text: Love performing? No

doing is carrying out or performing

clue.text: Knock fans' idol, showing guts? Impossible!

clue.text: Joyful expression initially gained by role playing

clue.text: African runners a source of mischief, sorry to say

clue.text: Game using cards as coins, strangely

parts.note: all the letters of the two words

clue.text: Reaction when men missing train?

clue.text: Tips from mathematicians show square and cube root
